# Create a custom Genmoji of a friend or pet for your next message

> **In short:** Genmoji is an Apple Intelligence feature that lets you turn a photo of someone in your Photos library (or a short text description) into a custom emoji you can send in Messages. You need an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 16, or newer, with iOS 18.2 or later and Apple Intelligence turned on.

By the end of this guide you'll be able to build a small, personalized emoji of a friend — or a text-described version of a pet — and send it inside an iMessage the same way you'd send a regular smiley face. We'll do the whole thing inside Apple's Messages app, so there's nothing extra to install.

## Before you start
- An **iPhone that supports Apple Intelligence** — currently the iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, the entire iPhone 16 lineup, and any newer model Apple has released since.
- **iOS 18.2 or later** installed (Genmoji arrived in the iOS 18.2 update).
- **Apple Intelligence turned on** in Settings → Apple Intelligence & Siri.
- At least one **clear, forward-facing photo of the person** saved in your Photos library. For pets, you'll use a text description instead — see Step 6.
- A few minutes. The whole flow is roughly **3 minutes** the first time, faster after that.

## Step 1 — Confirm Apple Intelligence is switched on
Open the **Settings** app (the gray gear icon on your home screen), then scroll down and tap **Apple Intelligence & Siri**. Make sure the toggle at the top says Apple Intelligence is on. If it asks you to wait in a queue, that just means your phone is still downloading the model — leave it plugged in and connected to Wi-Fi for a bit.

If you don't see **Apple Intelligence & Siri** in Settings, your iPhone or iOS version doesn't support the feature yet, and the rest of this guide won't work for you.
💬 Example: if Settings shows a message like *"Apple Intelligence is downloading…"*, leave the phone on the charger and check back in 15–30 minutes.
You'll know it worked when the toggle is green and the screen says Apple Intelligence is ready.

## Step 2 — Open Messages and tap into the text field
Open the **Messages** app (the green speech bubble icon). Tap the conversation you want to send to, or start a new one with the **pencil-and-paper icon** in the top-right corner. Then tap inside the message box at the bottom of the screen so the keyboard slides up.

You'll know it worked when the gray message box has a blue cursor blinking inside it and the regular letters keyboard is visible.

## Step 3 — Switch to the emoji keyboard
On the keyboard, find the **smiley-face icon** — usually bottom-left, sometimes to the right of the spacebar. Tap it once. The letters disappear and you're now in the emoji panel.

If your phone shows a globe 🌐 instead of a smiley, tap the smiley anyway; if that doesn't work, look for an **emoji or smiley** tab inside the keyboard's bottom row of icons.
You'll know it worked when you see rows of colorful emoji instead of letters.

## Step 4 — Find the Genmoji button
At the top of the emoji panel, look for a small **icon that looks like a smiley with a plus sign (+) or a sparkle** — Apple has changed this look between iOS versions, so it may also appear as a button labeled **Genmoji** or **Create**. Tap it.

If you don't see anything like that, swipe left on the row of category icons (clock, smileys, animals, food, activities) — Genmoji sometimes hides at the end.
You'll know it worked when a new screen appears with a text box that says something like *"Describe a Genmoji"*.

## Step 5 — Switch to the "Person" option for a friend's face
At the top of the Genmoji screen, look for two tabs or options: one for typing a description, and one for **choosing a person from your photos**. Tap the **person/photo** option. Your Photos library will open, and you'll see a row of faces Apple has recognized in your pictures. Tap the face of the friend you want to turn into a Genmoji.

If you don't see a "Person" option, your iOS version may not include that exact flow — in that case, skip to Step 6 and type a description of your friend instead.
💬 Example: tap the face labeled with your friend's name; Apple picks the most recent good photo automatically.
You'll know it worked when the Genmoji screen shows your friend's face as a small preview on the left or top of the screen.

## Step 6 — Add a description (and how to handle pets)
With a person selected, type a short description of what you want them doing or wearing in the Genmoji. This is also the place to come for **pets**, because there's no "Person" option for them — you just type what they look like and Apple generates a stylized version.

Keep the description short — one short sentence works best. Apple usually makes several options for you to swipe through.
💬 Example (friend): "wearing sunglasses and holding a coffee cup."
💬 Example (pet): "fluffy orange tabby cat with a tiny wizard hat."
You'll know it worked when a few generated Genmoji appear in a row on the screen, usually taking a second or two to appear.

## Step 7 — Pick your favorite and add it to the message
Swipe through the generated Genmoji and tap the one you like. Then look for a button like **Add** or simply tap the Genmoji itself — it should jump straight into your message box. Add any words around it, then tap the blue **send arrow** to deliver it.

If the Genmoji comes out as a **sticker-style** image instead of an inline emoji, long-press it in the message bubble to peel it off and drag it onto a different message — or just leave it as a sticker; the recipient can react to it.
You'll know it worked when your friend (or their chat) receives the message and the Genmoji appears as a small custom image inline or as a tappable sticker.

## Common mistakes
- **"I don't see a Genmoji button."** It's hidden behind the emoji keyboard, not in the regular letters keyboard. Make sure you're in the emoji panel (Step 3), then look for a smiley-with-plus or sparkle icon.
- **"The Person tab is empty."** Apple needs to have already recognized faces in your Photos. Open the Photos app, find a clear photo of the person, and tag their name in the People & Pets album. Come back and try again.
- **"I picked a pet photo and got nothing."** Pets aren't selectable in the Person tab. Use the **text description** option (Step 6) and describe them — color, breed, what's happening.
- **"The result looks nothing like my friend."** The first attempt is usually a stylized cartoon, not a portrait. Try a different source photo (front-facing, good lighting) or add a description like "smiling, glasses, short hair" to nudge the look.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** A quick way to make group chats feel personal — a custom Genmoji of your sister as a birthday cake decorator, your dog in a Halloween costume, or your running buddy in a raincoat.
- **For your business or work:** Drop a quick Genmoji of a teammate into Slack-style reactions (when shared as an image) or send a personalized thank-you in a work iMessage that actually feels like *you*, not a stock emoji.
- **If you're just getting started:** Stick to the simplest path: pick a person, add one short description, send the first result that makes you smile. You can experiment from there.

## Try it now
Open Messages, start a new text to a friend, switch to the emoji keyboard, tap the Genmoji button, and type: **"wearing pajamas and holding a mug of tea."** Pick the first option that makes you laugh, hit send, and watch the reaction roll in.
